title: Pay and Beyond: The Evolving Rewards for AI Skills
abstract: arXiv:2507.20410v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: This study examines the monetary and non-monetary rewards advertised in job vacancies requiring artificial intelligence skills in the U.S. labor market. Using approximately ten million online job vacancies posted between 2018 and 2025, we examine the development of AI demand, wage premia, and non-monetary benefits, including tuition assistance, paid leave, health and well-being programs, parental leave, inclusive workplace language, and remote work, across firms of different sizes. We find that demand for AI skills increased sharply following the introduction of generative AI in late 2022 across small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), large firms, and S&P 500 firms, while AI wage premia rose most strongly among SMEs. AI vacancies are significantly more likely than comparable non-AI roles to advertise non-monetary benefits, particularly remote work, inclusive culture, and parental leave. translated_title: 不止于薪酬：AI技能回报的演变
translated_abstract: 本研究考察了美国劳动力市场中要求人工智能技能的职位招聘所宣传的货币与非货币回报。利用2018年至2025年间发布的约一千万条在线职位招聘信息，我们研究了不同规模企业对AI人才需求的演变、工资溢价以及非货币福利（包括学费资助、带薪休假、健康与福祉项目、育儿假、包容性职场用语和远程办公）的发展。我们发现，自2022年底生成式AI问世以来，中小企业（SMEs）、大型企业以及标普500企业对AI技能的需求均急剧上升，其中中小企业的AI工资溢价涨幅最为显著。与可比的非AI岗位相比，AI岗位在招聘广告中宣传非货币福利的可能性显著更高，尤其是远程办公、包容性文化和育儿假。这一溢价在中小企业和大（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究基于2018-2025年间约一千万条美国职位招聘数据，发现生成式AI问世后各规模企业对AI技能的需求均大幅激增，AI岗位不仅享有工资溢价（在中小企业中最为突出），还更普遍地提供远程办公、包容性文化和育儿假等非货币福利。
en_tdlr: Drawing on about ten million U.S. job postings from 2018–2025, this study shows that demand for AI skills surged across firms of all sizes after the advent of generative AI in late 2022, with AI vacancies—especially at SMEs—offering both stronger wage premia and richer non-monetary benefits such as remote work, inclusive culture, and parental leave.
